sections.h2: How fast can I sell my house in Pearland, TX?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Pearland can close in a couple of weeks when the title is clean and the seller has the paperwork ready. A standard listing takes longer, because it adds showings, inspections and a buyer's loan approval.

Pearland has one feature that affects the paperwork: the city lies in three counties. Which county your lot is in decides where the deed is recorded and which tax office sends your bill, so confirm that first.

sections.h2: Which county is my Pearland house in?
sections.html:
Most likely Brazoria County, but not always. The city's finance page says Pearland is primarily in Brazoria County, with portions extending into Fort Bend and Harris counties, about 20 miles south of downtown Houston.

The same page lists the city's land area as 47.5 square miles and its population as approximately 132,900 as of January 1, 2024. Look at your tax bill or the appraisal district record to see the county. That tells you which clerk records the deed, which appraisal district values the house and which tax office collects.

  • Brazoria County: its tax office publishes payment options for homeowners.
  • Fort Bend County: ask that county's tax office and appraisal district for the bill and exemptions.
  • Harris County: its tax office publishes a detailed FAQ on penalties and closings.

sections.h2: What is Pearland's history, and why does it matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Pearland is a planned community that grew into a Houston suburb. The city's own history page says William Zychlinski bought 2,560 acres in 1892 around the Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe rail line and platted the town in 1894, naming east-west streets Walnut, Pear, Broadway, Jasmine, Plum and Orange.

Hurricanes shaped it. The 1900 storm destroyed nearly all of the early town and cut the population by almost three-quarters. A second hurricane in 1915 did similar damage, and the fig industry was the only one to grow afterward. The city incorporated in 1959, adopted a Home Rule Charter in February 1971, and uses a council-manager form of government.

For a seller the lesson is practical. Storm damage, drainage and flood insurance history are the questions buyers raise in a coastal area, so keep claims records and repair receipts together.

sections.h2: What tax payment options does Brazoria County offer?
sections.html:
For parcels in Brazoria County, the county tax office publishes several ways to pay over time. The table lists what its payment options page prints.

Brazoria County Tax Office payment options as printed on its site
OptionWho qualifiesDates printed
Split paymentAny propertyHalf by November 30, half by June 30
Four installmentsOver 65, disabled or disabled veteran homesteadsJanuary 31, March 31, May 31, July 31
Disaster installmentsDamaged property in a declared disaster areaJanuary 31, March 31, May 31, July 31
DeferralHomeowners 65 or older or disabledAffidavit filed; 5 percent interest per year
Partial paymentsAnyone unable to pay in fullAccepted in any amount

A deferral does not cancel the tax. It stays due, with interest, until the owner no longer owns and lives in the home, so a sale ends the deferral and the balance comes out of proceeds.

sections.h2: How are taxes settled when a Pearland house sells?
sections.html:
The title company prorates the current year and pays off anything delinquent. The Comptroller's state calendar sets the underlying rules: the lien attaches January 1, bills go out around October 1, and the penalty starts February 1 at 6 percent with 1 percent interest.

  • Ask the title company for a tax certificate for each county involved.
  • If your lender escrows taxes, tell the servicer your closing date so it can pay a bill that comes due around then.
  • Check homestead status. The state exemption is $140,000 for school taxes, and a buyer who takes title after January 1 may claim the exemption for the rest of the year if you did not.

These dates come from the Comptroller deadlines page. Ask the county tax office for any local rate or date.

sections.h2: Does a Pearland sale need extra steps for inherited or foreclosed property?
sections.html:
It can. An inherited house needs proof of who owns it before a buyer will close, and a house in foreclosure runs on a fixed auction schedule.

  • Inherited. Options on the State Law Library site include probate of a will, muniment of title, a small estate affidavit for estates of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead, and an affidavit of heirship.
  • Foreclosure. Auctions are on the first Tuesday of a month, and a notice of sale must be posted and filed at least 21 days before.
  • Deed recording. The county clerk of the county where the land sits files it, with $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 per added page.

See the State Law Library foreclosure guide for the stages.

faqs.a: Partly. The city is mainly in Brazoria County, with parts in Fort Bend and Harris counties. Your tax bill shows which county covers your lot.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair storm damage before I sell?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer will take the house as it is and price the work. Keep repair receipts and insurance claim records so you can describe the damage and fixes accurately.

faqs.q: Can I pay Pearland-area taxes in installments before selling?
faqs.a: In Brazoria County, yes, under the plans in the table above. The balance still comes out of proceeds if you sell, so ask for a payoff figure.

faqs.q: Who records the deed for a Pearland sale?
faqs.a: The county clerk where the house sits records it. The title company normally files it after closing and lists the fee on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: When does the tax penalty begin?
faqs.a: On February 1, according to the Comptroller, which prints a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest at that point. Ask the tax office about local dates.
